subject: Oceanography
title: La Niña
description: A micro-lesson that makes La Niña usable.

hook.text: La Niña is El Niño's opposite—trade winds strengthen and cold water dominates the eastern Pacific.

buildup.text: Stronger winds push more warm water westward—cold upwelling intensifies along the South American coast.

discovery.text: La Niña typically brings more Atlantic hurricanes, wetter conditions in Australia, and drought in the U.S. Southwest.

twist.text: La Niña events can persist for 2–3 years—unlike El Niño, which usually lasts one year.

climax.text: The 2020–2023 triple La Niña was exceptionally rare—causing record floods in Pakistan and Australian downpours.

punchline.text: El Niño's cold sibling can outstay her welcome—with global consequences.

quiz.question: How does La Niña affect Atlantic hurricanes?
